text:
Alice M: Heads-up: we're publishing SDK 12.0.0 today — a few breaking defaults (auth normalization, stricter bearer handling), retry/backoff behavior changes, and a new streaming resume API. Ping here if your app does any custom auth or streaming logic.

Ben K: Which auth changes specifically? header casing? any concrete migration snippet?

Danielle S: TL;DR: two user-facing auth changes — 1) the SDK no longer auto-prefixes tokens with `Bearer `; you must pass the full header or use the helper. 2) we tightened header parsing: previously we accepted implicit/loose tokens (any header name casing, or token in query), default is strict now. We provide `allow_legacy_auth: true` for an opt-in fallback but it's deprecated and will be removed in 13.x.

Danielle S: Migration examples — JS: 
```js
// old (worked if you passed just the token):
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
client.setAuth('mytoken123'); // used to auto-add "Bearer "

// new (explicit):
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
client.setAuth('Bearer mytoken123');
// or use helper that guarantees correct prefix:
client.setAuth(Redwood.formatBearer(process.env.RW_KEY));
```

Danielle S: Python: 
```py
# old: client.auth = os.environ['RW_KEY']
# new: client.auth = f"Bearer {os.environ['RW_KEY']}"
```

Evelyn T: Noted. Also saw streaming resumed differently in changelog — what should we change if we re-open streams after transient disconnects?

Danielle S: Streaming change: we added resume cursors + `onResume` hook. Previously teams re-opened a brand-new stream after a socket close which could lead to double-reading the last tokens or losing continuity. New recommended flow: persist the resume cursor from `stream.on('checkpoint', cursor)` and call `stream.resume(cursor)` on reconnect. Example: 
```js
stream.on('checkpoint', c => saveCursor(c))
// on reconnect:
const s = client.stream({ model: 'rw-7b' })
s.resume(loadCursor()) // server-side dedup ensures no double output
```

Frank L: About retries — do we require idempotency keys now? I noticed backoff is jittered by default.

Danielle S: Yes — policy changed: for non-GET operations we now recommend (and some client helpers require) `Idempotency-Key` for safe retries. Backoff algorithm moved from fixed -> exponential+full-jitter (to avoid thundering herds). The Node and Python clients include `IdempotencyKey` middleware that will auto-generate a UUID if you leave `idempotency: true`. But if you have side effects, explicitly provide a stable key.

Cait R: Runtime compatibility note: the serving layer accepts the new resume cursors and also honors `x-rw-model-profile` header (opt-in profiling). No functional break there, but Go SDK tests flagged header parsing differences (case-sensitive) — fyi.

Ben K: Can we toggle the strict auth behavior per environment (Dedicated/private customers)?

Danielle S: Yes — env var `RW_SDK_AUTH_STRICT=false` will restore legacy parsing for a limited window. For Dedicated we also added a feature flag in Console per org to enable legacy acceptance for a short rollback period. We're going to remove legacy after one-month ramp.

Alice M: I'll update migration checklist and add a repo scan job to find `setAuth(` without `Bearer`, and HTTP calls missing `Idempotency-Key`. @Danielle can you share the linter rule name so I can wire it into CI?

Danielle S: rule name: `rw_sdk/no_unprefixed_auth`. Quick scan example: `git grep -n "setAuth(\|Authorization:\s*[^B]" || true` — will catch likely offenders.

infra-bot: CI: node-sdk tests ✅, python-sdk tests ✅, go-sdk tests ❌ — failing due to header casing differences in x-go-http-client; rollback/shim PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/412 :eyes:

Grace P: Rollout plan? canary windows?

Danielle S: Plan: canary release (5% orgs) for 24h, monitoring for error spikes + resume failures + increased token duplication. If stable -> ramp to 50% next 24h -> 100% 48h after canary. Will publish a migration checklist and a small CLI scanner in the release notes. :rocket: :eyes:

Alice M: Thanks all — I'll post the checklist + links here when scrips land. If you have critical customers running custom auth/streaming, DM me so we can whitelist them on the legacy flag. :thumbsup:
